messages:
Maya R: Heads-up — staging showed a spike in exporter retries during a cluster scale-down window this morning. saw ~3x p99 retry rate for otlp-http.
Liam K: ack. any logs? were connections getting reset or were requests timing out and retried upstream?
Maya R: mostly connection resets + EOFs. traces show span export attempts stuck waiting on a conn that was closed by the kube iptables conntrack GC.
Samir: hmm, we had aggressive idle_conn_timeout in the previous rollout (10s) to free sockets fast. that might be racing with in-flight requests.
Eli: tradeoff: short idle frees resources quickly but increases chance of callers hitting closed sockets and triggering retries. longer idle reduces churn, higher fd usage.
Jon P: can we do graceful handoff: when scaling down we mark pool as draining and stop handing new requests but allow in-flight to finish with a generous deadline? avoids mid-flight EOFs.
Maya R: exactly what I was thinking. proposal:
```
exporter:
  conn_pool:
    max_idle: 50
    idle_timeout_ms: 30000
    drain_on_scale_down: true
  timeouts:
    dial_ms: 2500
    request_deadline_ms: 20000
  retry:
    budget_ms: 30000
    backoff_base_ms: 100
    jitter_pct: 0.2
```
Samir: +1 for drain_on_scale_down. also add a short grace window after K8S SIGTERM (eg 5s) before envoy/kube-proxy starts forcibly tearing sockets.
Liam K: what's the attacker surface for long idle? we could run out of fds on very high cardinality exporters. need a safe max_idle global.
Eli: we should make max_idle proportional to pool size and machine memory — defaults for small machines keep it low. also add passive healthchecks so bad upstreams get degraded earlier.
infra-bot: deploybot: rolled out exporter-pool-1config to staging at 2026-03-18T08:12:34Z
Jon P: after that deploy, can we add telemetry: metric exporter_pool.drain_count, exporter_conn.reset_rate, exporter_request.deadline_exceeded — to track regressions?
Maya R: yes adding those. would also like a dashboard row: retries vs drain events so we can correlate.
Samir: for retries, use a retry budget algorithm rather than naive infinite retries. budget per route per minute with soft cap and exponential backoff + jitter.
Liam K: for HTTP/2 specifically, we should also consider stream-level deadlines vs connection-level timeouts. if connection is reused but single stream fails, don't tear the conn.
Eli: good call. implement stream-level cancel and let connection remain healthy. only mark conn unhealthy after consecutive conn-level failures (3).
Maya R: I'll draft a small PR changing idle_timeout to 30s, add drain_on_scale_down + metrics + retry budget. will ping when ready for review.
Jon P: thanks — include a simple rollout plan: canary 10% pods, monitor exporter_conn.reset_rate and retry_rate for 1h before full rollout.
Maya R: plan noted. tagging @Liam K for final API knob names. :thumbsup:
Liam K: will review tonight. once merged, let's schedule the canary at low-traffic hours. :clock1:
